title: Veterans Pension Countable Income Terms by Rate Category
content:
# Countable income terms — Veterans Pension

## Spouse income

| Rate category | Spouse's income included in countable income |
|---|---|
| Veterans Pension (Basic Rate, No Dependents) | No |
| Veterans Pension (Basic Rate, One Dependent) | Yes |
| Veterans Pension (Housebound, No Dependents) | No |
| Veterans Pension (Housebound, One Dependent) | Yes |
| Veterans Pension (Aid and Attendance, No Dependents) | No |
| Veterans Pension (Aid and Attendance, One Dependent) | Yes |

## Income never counted (every rate category)

- Supplemental Security Income
- public assistance
- VA compensation paid to dependents
- life insurance proceeds, up to the final expenses

## Timing figures (every rate category)

| Item | Term |
|---|---|
| Months after the month an income change occurs before the adjusted rate is paid | 1 month |
| A decrease in countable income raises the rate | from the first of the month after the change |
| An increase in countable income lowers the rate | effective the last day of the month of the change |
| An adjustment reaching back over months already paid creates an overpayment debt | Yes |
| Days after VA's notice of an income-match discrepancy within which the veteran may respond before the proposed adjustment is made | 60 calendar days |
| Days after the income-match notice within which a hearing request delays the adjustment | 30 calendar days |

### Reading the terms (hypothetical dates)

- Income that fell during March: the higher rate applies from April 1, consistent with the one-month lag.
- Income that rose during March: the lower rate is effective March 31 and is paid from the following month.
- A one-dependent veteran whose spouse receives a pension of her own has that income counted; the same spouse income in a no-dependent category is not counted, because no spouse income is counted there.
